items.title: BREAKING: Copper prices on the LME have surged to a record $14,533 per ton, now up +47% over the last 12 months. The surge comes amid a supply shortage with rising demand from data centers, renewable energy, and power grids. Furthermore, expectations that President Trump will expand tariffs to refined copper imports have pushed US Comex prices above global prices. This is encouraging traders to ship hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US this year to profit from the price difference. Now, global stockpiles are increasingly concentrated in the US, draining LME inventories to critically low levels and leaving less copper readily available to buyers elsewhere. Copper's supply crunch

items.content:
US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate in years:

14.0% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in July, the highest rate since November 2023.

The national cancellation rate has held between 13.0% and 14.0% over the last 4 years, well above the lower rates typical of the seller's market from 2020 to 2022.

Atlanta posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.8%, followed by Houston at 19.6%, San Antonio at 18.7%, and Las Vegas at 18.6%.

This comes as sellers outnumber buyers by ~51%, near the highest percentage on record, giving buyers more options and making them more willing to walk away over inspection issues, low appraisals, or rejected concessions.

At the same time, high home prices and elevated mortgage rates are leaving buyers with less financial room, making unexpected costs or concerns about taking on large monthly payments more likely to derail deals.

The housing market is under historic pressure.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 8, 2026

items.title: Non-asset owners are very worried about inflation. The 3-month moving average of 1-year inflation expectations among US consumers with no stock holdings hit ~5.0% in August, near the highest level this year. This is significantly above the ~3.0% recorded in late 2024. Meanwhile, the 3-month moving average of inflation expectations among US consumers with the largest stock holdings remained below 4.0% last month. Readings for both groups were roughly in-line with levels seen in late-2022, following the recovery from the energy crisis. Asset owners are the only winners in this economy.

items.content:
BREAKING: The 4-week average of US new home listings rose +2.1% in the week ending August 30th, to 383,795, its highest since August 2022.

This exceeds this year’s previous peak of 383,712, set in April.

The increase was led by San Jose, Boston, and Nashville, where listings surged +29.4%, +26.1%, and +21.5%, respectively.

At the same time, the total number of homes for sale rose +0.4% to 1,511,313.

Meanwhile, pending home sales declined -0.1% over the same period to 308,282, the lowest since February, suggesting demand is failing to keep up with rising supply.

This comes as the median sale price rose +2.2% YoY to $398,632, while the average 30Y mortgage rate stood at 6.66%, near its highest over the last 12 months.

Housing market affordability is at record lows.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 7, 2026
